title: Julia language and scientific computing
summary: Julia from first scripts and data types to multiple dispatch, data workflows, numerical methods, optimization, performance and concurrent scientific programs, with offline executable examples.

lessons.title: First Julia scripts, values and observable output
lessons.outcome: Run a complete Julia script, trace bindings and distinguish a computed value from printed output.
lessons.lab: Use accepted 20 and rejected 3.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The total is 23. y remains 4.

lessons.title: Numbers, promotion, overflow and exactness
lessons.outcome: Choose and validate numeric representations while distinguishing exact arithmetic, overflow and floating-point approximation.
lessons.lab: Compute quotient and remainder for 7 divided by 2.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The integer quotient is 3 and remainder 1. The result equals 3//10 exactly.

lessons.title: Strings, Unicode and indexing boundaries
lessons.outcome: Process text without confusing byte positions, Unicode characters and visible grapheme clusters.
lessons.lab: Move from the first to the second character in the UTF-8 fixture.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: nextind returns 3.

lessons.title: Conditions, equality and explicit missing decisions
lessons.outcome: Write explicit Boolean decisions and select equality semantics appropriate to numeric values and data keys.
lessons.lab: Compare rates 0/5 and 0/0 under the helper policy.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The first is 0; the second is nothing.

lessons.title: Loops, ranges, comprehensions and scope
lessons.outcome: Trace finite iteration and scope rules while using explicit empty-input and indexing policies.
lessons.lab: List values from 1:3.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The range contains 1, 2 and 3. Use 3:-1:1.

lessons.title: Functions, keywords, closures and argument sharing
lessons.outcome: Write reusable functions with explicit contracts and distinguish local rebinding from mutation of a passed object.
lessons.lab: Call affine on 5 without keywords.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is 5. The result is 3.

lessons.title: Arrays, shapes, copies and views
lessons.outcome: Trace array storage and indexing while choosing deliberately between copies and shared views.
lessons.lab: Compare a length 2 vector with a 2-by-1 matrix.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: Their sizes are (2,) and (2, 1). It is at row 1, column 3.

lessons.title: Tuples, named records, dictionaries and sets
lessons.outcome: Choose collection representations according to identity, ordering, mutability and lookup needs.
lessons.lab: Represent a single integer as a tuple.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: Use (7,), including its comma. Counts are 1 and 2 while the set has two distinct labels.

lessons.title: Errors, tests and explicit input contracts
lessons.outcome: Validate scientific inputs, test expected failures and preserve unexpected errors instead of turning them into successful results.
lessons.lab: Calculate the mean of -1 and 1.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is the valid number 0.

lessons.title: Composite types, constructors and nested mutability
lessons.outcome: Use owned types to represent data contracts and distinguish immutable bindings from recursively immutable state.
lessons.lab: Attempt to construct a measurement with an unsupported unit.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: Its stored value is Float64.

lessons.title: Multiple dispatch and method specificity
lessons.outcome: Design generic operations over owned types and resolve overlapping method signatures explicitly.
lessons.lab: Construct a circle with radius 0.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: Its area is 0.

lessons.title: Parametric types and generic numerical code
lessons.outcome: Express useful type relationships without confusing subtype relations, storage representation or a method signature.
lessons.lab: Sum 1//3 and 2//3.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is exactly 1//1. The explicit additive identity is 0.

lessons.title: Broadcasting, axes and mutation order
lessons.outcome: Use broadcasting with explicit axes and distinguish an elementwise formula from a mutation-order-dependent algorithm.
lessons.lab: Add one offset per column to a matrix.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The example becomes [1, 1, 1, 1]. The example becomes [1, 1, 2, 3].

lessons.title: Missing values, absence and nonfinite measurements
lessons.outcome: Keep missingness and numerical failure distinct and report the denominator used by each aggregation policy.
lessons.lab: Summarize [1, missing, 3] using observed values.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: Total 3, observed 2 and mean 2. The mean becomes 4/3.

lessons.title: DataFrames transformations and grouped summaries
lessons.outcome: Transform a typed table and compute grouped summaries while preserving names, missingness and row counts.
lessons.lab: Scale the score column by 10 using ByRow.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The output column contains 1, 2 and 3 under the explicit name scaled. It reports 2 rows, 1 observed score and mean 1.

lessons.title: Joins, key validation and duplicate fanout
lessons.outcome: Validate relational assumptions in DataFrames joins and reconcile totals before and after a merge.
lessons.lab: Join the duplicated right-side entity 1 observations.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The left entity 1 weight appears twice. Two entity rows and weight total 300 are preserved.

lessons.title: Typed CSV input and round-trip data contracts
lessons.outcome: Parse and export bounded CSV data using explicit types and missingness rules rather than accidental inference.
lessons.lab: Read 001 as a declared string.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: Its leading zeros remain.

lessons.title: Dates, availability time and historical features
lessons.outcome: Use calendar arithmetic deliberately and reconstruct features using both event and availability time.
lessons.lab: Compare one month with thirty days from January 31 in the fixture.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: They end on February 29 and March 1. The fixture ends on March 29 versus March 31.

lessons.title: Linear algebra, conditioning and nonunique solutions
lessons.outcome: Solve small linear systems, inspect residuals and distinguish a fitted prediction from an identified coefficient vector.
lessons.lab: Multiply the computed vector by the original matrix.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The products are 7 and 3-2im.

lessons.title: Distributions, random state and Monte Carlo evidence
lessons.outcome: Use explicit random generators, compare simulation with analytic quantities and preserve the distinction between numerical and sampling uncertainty.
lessons.lab: Construct Normal(2, 3).
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The mean is 2 and variance 9.

lessons.title: Regression fitting, regularization and held-out assessment
lessons.outcome: Fit a small regression procedure with stable linear algebra and select regularization without using final outcomes.
lessons.lab: Fit the exact line without a penalty.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The coefficients are approximately [1, 2]. The selected penalty is 2.

lessons.title: Forward-mode automatic differentiation
lessons.outcome: Differentiate supported numerical functions and validate derivatives while preserving the numeric representation carried by dual numbers.
lessons.lab: Compute the gradient of x1 squared plus 3x2 squared at [2, 3].
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is [4, 18]. Gradients are [1, 1] and [0.5, 0.5].

lessons.title: Optimization objectives, constraints and convergence
lessons.outcome: Use a prepared optimization library while checking the objective, feasible set and independent convergence evidence.
lessons.lab: Replace a minimization objective with its negative.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The best feasible point is near 2.

lessons.title: Numerical methods, stability and error contracts
lessons.outcome: Compare explicit numerical approximations with known solutions and distinguish stability, positivity, residuals and position error.
lessons.lab: Compare Euler with 4 and 20 steps for rate 1.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The fine final value is closer to exp(-1). The refined approximation is closer to 1/3.

lessons.title: Inference, profiling and measured performance
lessons.outcome: Explain which work a timing includes, inspect type inference and measure a small kernel without turning machine-dependent timing into a correctness assertion.
lessons.lab: Trace total after each element of [1.0, 2.0, 3.0].
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The values are 1, 5 and 14. The result is Float32(5).

lessons.title: Allocation, mutation and alias-safe numerical work
lessons.outcome: Implement a preallocated matrix step, explain ownership and aliasing, and compare semantic results before measuring storage behavior.
lessons.lab: Compute the two entries before running the first case.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The final vector is [11, 11]. The new vector is [5, 5].

lessons.title: Modules, source loading and reproducible projects
lessons.outcome: Separate namespaces from source files, execute a tiny owned multi-file project offline, and distinguish locked dependencies from code loading.
lessons.lab: Call LocalStats.center on [2, 4].
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is [-1, 1].

lessons.title: Property testing and reproducible numerical evidence
lessons.outcome: Combine hand-derived cases, generated inputs and invariants so that a plausible but incorrect transformation cannot pass by comparing only to itself.
lessons.lab: Compute probabilities for weights [2, 5, 3] by hand.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is [0.2, 0.5, 0.3]. The sum exceeds Float64 range.

lessons.title: Tasks, channels and bounded asynchronous pipelines
lessons.outcome: Build a bounded producer-consumer pipeline, join its work and explain how asynchronous scheduling differs from simultaneous CPU execution.
lessons.lab: Describe what happens when a producer fills a capacity-two buffer.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is [4, 0, 9].

lessons.title: Threads, ownership and deterministic reductions
lessons.outcome: Run independent chunks on the prepared two-thread runtime, combine results deterministically and protect shared state with an explicit lock.
lessons.lab: Compute the sum of squares through 100 from the closed-form formula.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The result is 338350. The empty range contributes 0.

lessons.title: Expressions, hygienic macros and C interoperability
lessons.outcome: Inspect syntax without evaluating untrusted text, implement a hygienic single-evaluation macro and call a precisely typed Linux C function.
lessons.lab: Identify the head and first argument of parsed 1 + 2.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: The head is :call and the function symbol is :+. The counter would be 2.

lessons.title: Scientific capstone: an auditable offline modeling report
lessons.outcome: Execute a complete synthetic modeling workflow from typed CSV to a source-identified decision record, exact numerical checks and an accessible Plotly report.
lessons.lab: Explain what one row and one ID represent.
lessons.verification: Reproduce the stated observations, for example: Penalty 2 is selected. Residuals are -1/7 and -2/7; MSE is 5/98.
